content: Signature 1932 is a premium, hand-crafted cigar brand owned by the Padilla Cigar Company, based in Hialeah, Florida. The brand was created by José Pepin Garcia and is primarily manufactured at the El Rey de los Habanos factory located in the Little Havana neighborhood of Miami, Florida. However, one specific size, known as La Perla, is produced at Tabacalera Cubana S.A. (TACUBA), Pepin Garcia's factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. The brand was named as a tribute to the late Heberto Padilla, a renowned Cuban poet born in 1932, by his son Ernesto Padilla, the owner of Padilla Cigars. The release of the brand was carried out in stages. The first three vitolas—Robusto, Churchill, and Torpedo—were introduced in October 2006. These cigars were packaged in special cedar boxes containing 45 cigars (15 of each size), with only 500 boxes produced. These boxes were designed to remain on display and be refilled with subsequent shipments. The next phase of the release began in January 2007 with the introduction of the Toro size. In February 2007, the Lancero size and a second release of the previously launched sizes followed, all packaged in Cuban-style boxes of 25 cigars. The third size, La Perla, was delayed and eventually released in late March or early April 2007, marking the start of the brand's regular production. The Signature 1932 line has received notable recognition. The Churchill size was awarded a rating of 90 in the December 2006 issue of Cigar Aficionado magazine and was named the 14th best cigar of 2006 by the same publication. Additionally, it was designated Cigar of the Week for the week of January 20, 2007. The Robusto size received a rating of 88 in the February 2007 issue of Cigar Aficionado. The La Perla size earned a rating of 90 in the May 8, 2007 issue of Cigar Insider. The Signature 1932 line consists of six vitolas in total. The cigars feature a Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper and Nicaraguan Criollo filler and binder. They are packaged in Cuban-style boxes of 25 cigars. The La Perla size is unique within the line, as it is the smallest, comes unbanded, is packaged in cabinets of 50, and is the only vitola produced in Nicaragua at TACUBA. Production of La Perla is limited. The cigar band of the Signature 1932 is a highly intricate and artistic design. It features a maroon background with elaborate gold borders and scrollwork. The left wing of the band displays the words Little Havana (brk) Miami in gold, while the right wing ends with an ornate P monogram and includes the words Cuban Crafted along with the lot number, both in gold. The center of the band showcases the detailed Padilla monogram at the top, followed by the name Padilla, the word Signature in script, and 1932. At the bottom of the center section is the Cuban coat of arms.
